title: FastAPI Realtime and Files: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before notes on FastAPI WebSocket endpoints, disconnect handling and broadcasting, then StreamingResponse, server-sent events, file responses and UploadFile uploads.

chapters.title: WebSockets and Streaming: The Mental Model
points: A WebSocket is one persistent, full-duplex TCP connection upgraded from HTTP, so server and client can send at any time; plain HTTP is one request and one response
Declare it with @app.websocket('/ws') on async def f(websocket: WebSocket); path, query, header and cookie params work like normal routes, but there is no response_model and no status code
StreamingResponse takes a generator and sends chunks as they are produced, so the whole body is never held in memory
Server-sent events (SSE) are one-way server to browser over plain HTTP with media type text/event-stream; the browser EventSource reconnects automatically
UploadFile is a spooled temp file: small uploads stay in memory, large ones roll over to disk

chapters.title: WebSocket Endpoint Workflow
points: Handshake first: await websocket.accept() must run before any send or receive; sending or receiving first raises RuntimeError and Uvicorn answers the handshake with a 500, while close() before accept() rejects it with a 403
Receive with receive_text(), receive_bytes() or receive_json(); each awaits the next message
Send with send_text(), send_bytes() or send_json(data)
Echo loop: await websocket.accept(); while True: data = await websocket.receive_text(); await websocket.send_text(f'You said: {data}')
Close from the server with await websocket.close(code=1000); 1008 means policy violation and is the usual code for failed auth

chapters.title: Disconnects and Broadcasting
points: A client leaving makes the next receive raise WebSocketDisconnect (from fastapi), so wrap the loop in try/except WebSocketDisconnect
Always clean up in except or finally: remove the socket from your connection list, or dead sockets pile up and later sends fail
Connection manager pattern: a class holding active: list[WebSocket] with async connect (accept and append), disconnect (remove) and broadcast (for ws in active: await ws.send_text(msg))
Broadcast to a copy, iterate list(self.active), and drop sockets whose send raises, since removing from a list while iterating skips entries
The manager lives in one process only; with several workers or servers you need Redis pub/sub or similar to broadcast across them

chapters.title: StreamingResponse and Server-Sent Events
points: StreamingResponse(generator(), media_type='text/plain') accepts a sync or async generator, and an async def generator with yield is preferred so the event loop is not blocked
A sync generator is run in a threadpool, but time.sleep or blocking calls inside an async generator freeze every request, so use await asyncio.sleep
SSE wire format: each event is 'data: <payload>\n\n', and the blank line ends the event; optional fields are event:, id: and retry:
SSE endpoint: StreamingResponse(gen(), media_type='text/event-stream') with headers Cache-Control: no-cache and X-Accel-Buffering: no so nginx does not buffer the stream
Client side: new EventSource('/events') with onmessage; EventSource is GET only and cannot send custom headers, which makes auth awkward, so use WebSocket or fetch streaming when you need that

chapters.title: File Responses and UploadFile
points: FileResponse(path, filename='report.pdf') streams a file from disk, sets Content-Length, Content-Type and Content-Disposition, and supports Range requests
Never pass user-supplied paths straight to FileResponse, because path traversal like ../../etc/passwd leaks files, so resolve the path and check it stays inside your base directory
Single upload: async def up(file: UploadFile) reads multipart form data; list[UploadFile] accepts several; both need the python-multipart package installed

UploadFile attributes are filename, content_type and file, with async read(size), write(), seek() and close(); calling await file.read() on a huge file loads it all into RAM, so read in chunks such as while chunk := await file.read(1024*1024)

UploadFile versus bytes: bytes = File() reads everything into memory, UploadFile spools to disk; use UploadFile for anything large, and never trust file.filename or content_type, so validate size and type and generate your own saved name

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Realtime and Files
points: WebSocket: accept(), receive_text/bytes/json(), send_text/bytes/json(), close(code=1000), catch WebSocketDisconnect, remove the socket in finally
Broadcast: manager with active list, iterate a copy, prune failed sends, use Redis pub/sub for multiple workers
Stream: StreamingResponse(async_gen(), media_type=...) and never block inside the generator
SSE: media_type='text/event-stream', frames 'data: x\n\n', Cache-Control: no-cache, EventSource is GET only
Files: FileResponse(path, filename=...) with a validated path; UploadFile with chunked read(), python-multipart installed, validate name, type and size
